questions.text: What is the minimum mobilization component payable upon signing under UAP Document 401-402 Article 3.02?

rationale.a: The checked article gives a higher stated minimum.
rationale.b: Article 3.02 states a minimum of PHP 25,000.00 upon signing as the mobilization component of the Architect fee.
rationale.c: 15.0% is the schematic-design cumulative payment milestone, not the signing mobilization minimum.
rationale.d: 85.0% is reached at Contract Documents and adjusted after award.
rationale.correct: Article 3.02 states a minimum of PHP 25,000.00 upon signing as the mobilization component of the Architect fee.
rationale.takeaway: Separate signing mobilization from later cumulative percentage milestones.

questions.text: At completion of Schematic Design Services, total payment is brought to what cumulative amount?

options.text: 15.0% of the Basic Fee, less the mobilization already paid
The full balance based on FPCC

rationale.a: Article 3.02 brings total payment to 15.0% of the Basic Fee after Schematic Design, less the mobilization already paid.
rationale.b: 35.0% is the Design Development cumulative milestone.
rationale.c: 85.0% is the Contract Documents cumulative milestone.
rationale.d: Final balance is paid upon completion of work.
rationale.correct: Article 3.02 brings total payment to 15.0% of the Basic Fee after Schematic Design, less the mobilization already paid.
rationale.takeaway: These percentages are cumulative, not standalone phase slices.

questions.text: After Design Development Services are completed, total payments increase to what cumulative amount?

rationale.b: 20.0% is not the source wording in Article 3.02.
rationale.c: Article 3.02 states that completion of Design Development increases total payment to 35.0% of the Basic Fee.
rationale.correct: Article 3.02 states that completion of Design Development increases total payment to 35.0% of the Basic Fee.
rationale.takeaway: Answer with the cumulative total stated by the source.

questions.text: After Contract Documents Services are completed, total payments increase to what cumulative amount?

rationale.a: 35.0% is the Design Development cumulative milestone.
rationale.c: Article 3.02 states that completion of Contract Documents increases total payment to 85.0% of the Basic Fee.
rationale.d: The remaining balance is not fully due at Contract Documents.
rationale.correct: Article 3.02 states that completion of Contract Documents increases total payment to 85.0% of the Basic Fee.
rationale.takeaway: Contract Documents is the major cumulative billing milestone.

questions.text: After award to the winning constructor-bidder, what adjustment does Article 3.02 require?

options.text: Total payment is adjusted to 85.0% of the Basic Fee computed on the lowest bona fide bid or winning bid price
The fee is fixed forever to the schematic SPPCC

rationale.a: Article 3.02 adjusts payment after award so the total equals 85.0% of the Basic Fee computed on the lowest bona fide bid or winning bid price.
rationale.b: The source does not cancel prior payments.
rationale.c: Article 3.02 includes an adjustment tied to the bid price.
rationale.d: The source keeps a remaining 15.0% framework.
rationale.correct: Article 3.02 adjusts payment after award so the total equals 85.0% of the Basic Fee computed on the lowest bona fide bid or winning bid price.
rationale.takeaway: Bid-stage adjustment is still tied to the 85.0% cumulative milestone.

questions.text: How is the remaining 15.0% of the Architect fee handled after the 85.0% milestone?

options.text: It is handled through progress billing and final balance based on completion/FPCC language
It is paid only if the Owner requests extra services

rationale.a: The source does not forfeit the remaining fee.
rationale.b: Article 3.02 says the remaining 15.0% is progress billed, and the balance is paid upon completion based on FPCC.
rationale.c: The remaining fee is part of regular fee payment, not only extra services.
rationale.d: Architect fee balance is not contractor retention.
rationale.correct: Article 3.02 says the remaining 15.0% is progress billed, and the balance is paid upon completion based on FPCC.
rationale.takeaway: Do not stop the payment schedule at 85.0%.

questions.text: In Article 7.08, what does the remaining 15.0% represent after the Contract Documents Phase?

options.text: 10.0% for Article 1723 liability and 5.0% for construction phase service
5.0% for liability and 10.0% for bidding only
A penalty retained by the Owner

rationale.a: Article 7.08 breaks the remaining 15.0% into 10.0% for Article 1723 liability and 5.0% for construction phase service.
rationale.b: Schematic design is not the remaining 15.0% after Contract Documents.
rationale.c: The source states the opposite split.
rationale.d: The source treats this as remaining service/liability value, not a penalty.
rationale.correct: Article 7.08 breaks the remaining 15.0% into 10.0% for Article 1723 liability and 5.0% for construction phase service.
rationale.takeaway: The 85/15 structure has a source-stated rationale.

questions.text: Which reading of Article 3.02 is safest for board computation?

options.text: Each design phase has a separate standalone percentage unrelated to prior payments
The percentages are cumulative totals reached at each milestone
The Owner pays all fees only at project completion
The Architect may ignore prior mobilization payments

rationale.a: Article 3.02 repeatedly says payment increases total payments to the stated percentage.
rationale.b: The Article 3.02 language is cumulative: each milestone increases total payments to the stated percentage.
rationale.c: The source includes staged payments before completion.
rationale.d: The schematic payment is reduced by the mobilization already paid.
rationale.correct: The Article 3.02 language is cumulative: each milestone increases total payments to the stated percentage.
rationale.takeaway: Compute the current amount due by subtracting prior payments from the cumulative entitlement.

questions.text: What timing phrase appears for Schematic, Design Development, and Contract Documents payment after submission?

options.text: Not more than 15 days after submission
Only after the contractor submits a bid bond

rationale.a: Article 3.02 uses the phrase not more than 15 days after submission for the Schematic, Design Development, and Contract Documents milestones.
rationale.b: The source uses a much shorter payment timing phrase.
rationale.c: The source creates milestone payments before final completion.
rationale.d: Bid bonds are not the payment timing trigger in Article 3.02.
rationale.correct: Article 3.02 uses the phrase not more than 15 days after submission for the Schematic, Design Development, and Contract Documents milestones.
rationale.takeaway: The due date is tied to completion/submission of the relevant service milestone.
